tasks.short: Plan and revise physics curricula and instruction

steps.what: Evaluate the existing physics curriculum, course content, materials and methods using actual student work, course evaluations and colleague observations, distinguishing evidence of misunderstanding from unsupported impressions.

Plan and select revisions to physics curricula, course content and instructional methods, deciding conceptual prerequisites, mathematical depth, laboratory links and suitable examples with relevant colleagues.

Map the selected topics, prerequisite links and activities into the course structure in {LMS}; configure native course-map and resource-reference views to reduce repeated link assembly, checking every proposed mapping against the teacher's selected revisions.

Revise the actual physics explanations, examples, laboratory references and method notes in {LMS}; reuse native reference and formatting fields for repeated assembly, then check the complete final draft for physical meaning, mathematical consistency and alignment with the selected course map.
Commit the checked revised course draft in the staff development area of {LMS} for the existing curriculum review process.

tasks.design: Configure native course maps and reference fields in {LMS}. The teacher evaluates learning evidence, selects curriculum changes and writes and checks the actual physics content; native reuse reduces repeated links and formatting only.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course revision can repeat prerequisite links and resource references across sections.
tasks.enabler_now: Native course structures can reuse explicit topic and resource relationships.
tasks.still_hard: Choose the right conceptual progression and verify physical and mathematical meaning.
tasks.human_edge: Connect students' actual difficulties with sound physics teaching.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated course assembly with unchanged curriculum responsibility.

evidence.claim: Native course maps and resource fields can reduce repeated link and format assembly without evaluating physics teaching quality.

assumptions: Boundary is evaluation and revision through the stored internal course draft; programme approval and student-facing publication remain existing downstream actions, with no saving claimed there. Shares are illustrative.

Programme owner supplies approved goal IDs and curriculum version; existing course records supply topic/resource IDs and original materials. Teacher obtains and evaluates actual course evidence in s1 and chooses revisions in s2. Missing links and evidence require manual source checking and discussion counted in s1-s3, not generated learner judgements.

Native course reuse precedes code. Only repeated mapping/reference assembly and formatting lose time; substantive content writing, physical reasoning and mathematical checking remain. Existing system runtime earns no credit. s4 contains the ordinary completed-draft check with no extra self-approval time; edits invalidate the commit gate.
research_questions: Which repeated links and reference fields remain manual after native course configuration?

already_counted.description: Evidence evaluation, revision decisions, retained mapping, actual writing/check and commit remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Maintain topic links and test reused reference fields after course changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final internal revised physics course draft checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 11.6 less 2 upkeep gives 9.6. Upper range 9 removes repeated links and formatting; zero if native reuse already works.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the actual physics laboratory setup, exercise instructions, equipment condition and student readiness before the supervised work begins, clarifying any unresolved practical or safety constraint.

Supervise students' laboratory work, observe actual experimental technique, question interpretations, respond to unsafe practice and help students distinguish a measurement problem from a physical effect.
Write the required factual supervision or exception note in the existing laboratory teaching record {LMS}, then check the completed entry against actual observations and any required follow-up.
Commit the checked factual supervision entry in the existing laboratory teaching record {LMS}.

tasks.design: Keep laboratory readiness checks and supervision human. Existing {LMS} record entry already supports the separate factual note; no new automation or saving is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practical supervision depends on actual experiments and student behaviour.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record functions are sufficient; no new enabler is claimed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise an unsafe setup or a misleading measurement in real time.
tasks.human_edge: Guide experimental reasoning while protecting practical safety.

ambition.what: No automatic laboratory or student decisions.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in laboratory supervision duties.

reach.learn: Observation, escalation and factual laboratory notes

evidence.claim: Existing teaching records can hold factual laboratory notes without replacing direct experimental supervision.

assumptions: Boundary includes this teacher's readiness check, actual supervision and existing required factual note. Separate student grading, equipment repair and incident escalation receive no saving here. Shares are illustrative over the supervision work; no note is fabricated for every exchange.

Exercise owner supplies instruction version and recording criteria; actual equipment and students supply the observed context. Teacher checks it in s1-s2 and writes actual findings in s3. Missing facts require direct observation or clarification counted there, not inference from scheduled attendance.

Native recording was considered. After separating the actual note and save, no removable duplicate work was found. Record creation and the real same-system save retain full effort. s3 contains the ordinary final-entry check without added self-approval time; edits invalidate the commit gate. No change means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Focal teacher and assistant supervision boundaries
research_questions: Does any genuine duplicate note entry exist outside the current native record?

already_counted.description: Readiness, live supervision, actual note/check and commit remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: No proposed change introduces additional upkeep.

approvals.approved_version: Actual completed supervision note checked in s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All actual readiness, supervision and separate factual record work retain full time; no changed manual action has been established.

steps.what: Find current physics literature through scholarly discovery and reference-management software {OTHER}; configure native topic searches and duplicate filters to reduce repeated catalogue navigation, checking original titles, authors and relevance.
Read current physics literature in full where relevant, examine its assumptions, methods and results and assess how a claimed development changes the teacher's understanding.

Keep abreast of developments by talking with colleagues and participating in professional conferences, questioning interpretations and comparing new physics results with actual research and teaching experience.

tasks.design: Configure native scholarly searches in discovery software {OTHER}. Reduce repeated finding and duplicate screening while retaining source reading, colleague exchange and conference participation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Following several scholarly sources repeats catalogue searching.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches can reuse explicit topic criteria and bibliographic identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Assess whether a result is credible, novel and relevant.
tasks.human_edge: Question the physical assumptions and connect research with teaching.
tasks.altitude: Less literature navigation with unchanged critical reading and professional exchange.

evidence.claim: Native scholarly searches and bibliographic duplicate filters can reduce repeated discovery without establishing the scientific validity of a paper.

assumptions: Boundary is discovery, actual reading and professional exchange, not conference purchasing/registration, a written literature review or bibliography production. No routine report, send or record commit is required by this statement. Shares are illustrative.

Scholarly publishers and catalogues supply title, authors, date, identifiers and source access; teacher provides actual interests and search terms in s1. Missing metadata requires original-source lookup counted in s1. No generated summary substitutes for reading.

Native discovery features precede code. Existing indexing runtime earns no labour credit; only repeated human searching and duplicate screening lose time. All source evaluation, discussion and conference participation retain full effort.
research_questions: Do existing topic filters already remove repeat searching without excluding relevant physics work?

already_counted.description: Search verification, original reading and professional exchange remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: Review topic filters and check missed or irrelevant results.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10 less 1 upkeep gives 9. Zero for already effective native searches; upper case removes repeated discovery only.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate on teaching and research issues

steps.what: Retrieve the relevant physics teaching or research issue records and source files in {PROJECT} and {DOCS}; configure native issue-to-source links to reduce repeated navigation, checking the current version and actual unresolved question.

Collaborate with colleagues to address teaching and research issues, compare interpretations, work through the actual physics or pedagogical problem and agree the next investigation or teaching action.
outputs: agreed issue findings and next actions

steps.what: Write the actual issue findings, uncertainties and agreed action owners in {PROJECT}, then check the completed record against the discussion and supporting evidence.
inputs: agreed issue findings and next actions

steps.what: Commit the checked final issue findings and action record in {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure native issue-to-source links in {PROJECT} and {DOCS}. Keep the collaboration and actual findings write, reducing repeated context retrieval before the separate final-record commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: A discussion may require locating the same issue sources repeatedly.
tasks.enabler_now: Native issue links can expose the current source records.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve a disputed interpretation or choose a worthwhile next investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Combine colleagues' expertise and acknowledge unresolved evidence.

ambition.what: No additional research or teaching decision rights.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated context retrieval with unchanged collaboration duties.

reach.task: Discuss a recurring physics teaching issue

evidence.claim: Native issue-source links can reduce repeated retrieval while substantive scientific discussion and findings writing remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary is issue-focused collaboration and its actual action record, not curriculum revision in task 5924 or general professional exchange in 5923. No shared action is claimed twice. Colleague effort is not claimed or transferred. Shares are illustrative.

Existing issue owner supplies issue ID, open question, source IDs/revisions and access. Teacher verifies the actual context in s1, resolves missing sources through manual lookup or clarification there and produces findings with colleagues in s2. No free prepared issue summary is assumed.

Native issue links precede code. Only repeated source navigation loses time, not substantive source reading, discussion or actual record writing. Same-system saving keeps full time. s3 contains the ordinary completed-record check without added self-approval labour; edits invalidate the requested commit gate.
research_questions: Which sources are repeatedly located before the same issue discussions?

already_counted.description: Retained source verification, collaboration, actual findings/check and commit remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain issue-source links and resolve changed references.

approvals.approved_version: Final issue findings, uncertainties and action owners checked in s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 4.5 less 1 upkeep gives 3.5. Zero for already effective issue links; upper case removes repeated source navigation only.
